verdict.rationale: Factory documents its own background-automation capabilities: "persistent automations" in Software Factory, code review, QA, and docs "on autopilot," and event-triggered remote delegation from Linear and Jira issues. It also offers headless `droid exec` with tiered autonomy for CI/CD and scripts, and automated PR review that posts inline comments. However, the automation setup surface is thin: there is no documented scheduler or recurring-trigger configuration, and `droid exec` is a one-shot command that relies on external CI or scripts to run repeatedly. missing for 10: documented automation creation/configuration flow, native recurring schedules or cron-style triggers, independent or hands-on corroboration that automations run unattended.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: live metrics, connected integrations, repository coverage, stage health, and persistent automations
Put code review, QA, and documentation on autopilot across your repos.
Assign a Linear issue to Factory or mention `@Factory` in an issue comment to have Droid investigate, implement, and test the work.
Droid analyzes pull requests and merge requests, identifies issues, and posts feedback as inline comments.
Droid Exec is Factory's headless execution mode designed for automation workflows.
Droid exec uses tiered autonomy to control what operations can run without manual confirmation.
